title: Sharpe ratio and the annualisation identities around it
source:
"""Daily and annualised Sharpe with the two different scaling laws.

excess = strategy - risk_free (daily, simple)
mean and std (ddof=1) of the excess; sharpe_daily = mean / std
annualised: mean * 252 (linear), std * sqrt(252), sharpe * sqrt(252)
The identity sharpe_annualised == annualised_excess_return / annualised_volatility
is asserted, because it is exactly what separates the two conventions.
"""
import json
import math
import os

import pandas as pd

INPUT = "/input/environment/data/daily.parquet"
OUT = "/app/output/performance.json"
DAYS = 252


def main() -> None:
    df = pd.read_parquet(INPUT)
    excess = (df["strategy_return"].astype(float) - df["risk_free_daily"].astype(float)).dropna()
    mean = float(excess.mean())
    std = float(excess.std(ddof=1))
    perf = {
        "n_days": int(len(excess)),
        "mean_daily_excess": mean,
        "std_daily_excess": std,
        "sharpe_daily": mean / std,
        "sharpe_annualised": mean / std * math.sqrt(DAYS),
        "annualised_volatility": std * math.sqrt(DAYS),
        "annualised_excess_return": mean * DAYS,
    }
    assert abs(perf["sharpe_annualised"]
               - perf["annualised_excess_return"] / perf["annualised_volatility"]) < 1e-12
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(OUT), exist_ok=True)
    with open(OUT, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(perf, fh, indent=2)
    with open(OUT, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        assert set(json.load(fh)) == set(perf)
    print(perf)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
